subject: SparrowTech hosted endpoint: residency, retention & purge Qs
messages:
From: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@sparrowtech.com>

Subject: SparrowTech hosted endpoint questionnaire — residency & purge

Hi Priyom —

Attached is a short questionnaire from our privacy/compliance team focused on data residency and deletion for the hosted API. Two quick asks: can you confirm your standard retention windows and the SLO for issuing a verified tenant data purge? Also we need a short note on how snapshots/backups are handled (are they covered by the same erase SLO?).

We'd like answers we can share with our Legal and InfoSec review this week.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Rivers
Head of Product Security, SparrowTech

From: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
To: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@sparrowtech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-11-29T10:20:00Z
Subject: Re: SparrowTech hosted endpoint questionnaire — residency & purge

Alex —

Thanks for sending this over. Below are consolidated answers we can provide to InfoSec. I've attached a short retention matrix and a one-page SOP for tenant erasures. If you want a formal attestation we can include our standard language for the contract addendum.

Summary (hosted API):
- Default customer data retention: 30 days for request payload and model outputs (logically deletable on request).
- Optional ephemeral mode: 0-day persistence available for enterprise customers via an account flag; this disables long-term logging of request/response bodies.
- Audit logs & metadata: audit trails (request IDs, timestamps, routing metadata) retained for 365 days to support security investigations; these do not include full request payloads when ephemeral mode is enabled.
- Backup snapshots: system backups that may contain encrypted snapshots of active state are retained up to 90 days. Backups are included in erasure SLOs; we run a coordinated purge across snapshots and live storage when a tenant-level erasure is requested.
- Erasure SLO: verified tenant-level erasure completed within 30 days by default; 10 business-day expedited option available under enterprise contracts. Erasure steps include: live-data purge, KV/prefix cache invalidation, snapshot purge, and verification run with audit log entry.

Notes on deletion mechanics:
- Deletions are done via a multi-phase pipeline to avoid partial exposure: (1) mark objects for deletion and record operation in the audit log, (2) remove primary objects and KV cache entries, (3) schedule snapshot/backup purge job tied to snapshot lifecycle, (4) run verification scan and publish a signed deletion report.
- Encryption: hosted API data at rest is encrypted with service-managed KMS keys by default; we offer a customer-managed KMS option for enterprise customers. Keys are rotated and envelope-encrypted; we can provide key-rotation logs on request under NDA.

I've included Ben and Monica to help coordinate a short evidence pack if InfoSec wants examples (SOP, deletion report template, sample audit log entry).

Best,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-retention-matrix-2028.csv, sop-tenant-erasures-summary.pdf]

Adding a quick security clarification for the InfoSec team:

- Snapshots/backups: snapshots are immutable once written; our purge pipeline will mark and remove any snapshots that contain tenant data, but due to distributed replication the purge job is eventually consistent across regions. We verify removal via hash-based scans and list reconciliation; verification artifacts are retained in the audit logs.
- Cache vs KV: short-term in-memory caches (sub-second TTL) are not captured in backups and are ephemeral. The KV cache that powers prompt prefix caching is persisted to disk for warm-starts and is treated like primary storage in erasure flows.
- Third-party storage: we use cloud provider-managed block stores for hosted storage; access is restricted to the runtime service account. No external vendor has direct tenant-level access.

If Sparrow wants a formal timeline for the expedited 10-business-day erasure, we will need a signed amendment that specifies the customer account and required notification window.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. Two clarifying questions from our Legal/Security: (1) when you say backups are included in erasure SLOs, do you mean they will be purged from all provider snapshots (including cold-region replicas) or only from live-region snapshots? (2) can you confirm whether audit logs containing request IDs are ever able to be re-linked to raw request payloads after an erasure is performed? We need to understand re-identification risk.

We'd also like an example of the signed deletion report you referenced.

Alex

From: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
To: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@sparrowtech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, irene_choi@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-11-30T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SparrowTech hosted endpoint questionnaire — residency & purge

Alex —

Answers to your clarifying questions:

1) Backup/snapshot coverage: our documented erasure pipeline targets all storage tiers that could reasonably contain tenant data: live-region volumes, cold-region replicas, and managed snapshot stores. Practically, that means the purge job enqueues deletion for replicas and snapshots across provider regions; final consistency is subject to snapshot retention windows and the cloud provider's internal garbage collection. We include a reconciliation step that lists remaining objects and triggers provider-side support tickets if any replica remains beyond the expected window.

2) Audit logs and re-linking risk: audit logs contain request identifiers, timestamps, and routing metadata but not full request payloads when the tenant is in ephemeral mode. After a verified erasure we run a re-link check: we attempt to correlate remaining log entries with any stored payload indices. If payloads were deleted correctly there will be no retrievable raw payloads to re-link to. The audit log entry for the erasure itself documents the scope and outcome; that log entry is retained to prove the operation occurred.

Attached is a redacted example of the signed deletion report (SOP includes the template). If Sparrow requires forensic evidence for compliance, we can provide a signed report with hash digests of deleted manifests under an evidence-sharing NDA.

Next steps: Ben can schedule a short call with our compliance engineering team to walk InfoSec through the verification artifacts — are you available tomorrow at 14:00 PT?

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
